title: Security & downloads
detail: Engine and mod downloads are checked against pinned SHA-256 hashes before installation. That verifies expected bytes; it is not a promise that third-party software is malware-free.
steam: SteamCMD is Valve’s official downloader. Its bootstrap comes from Valve’s HTTPS CDN; later updates and owned game downloads are handled by Valve’s updater.
mods: Generals mods use reviewed data-file manifests rather than downloaded mod installers. Some files come from an HTTP community mirror with pinned hashes. Other engines and native mods come from their published releases.
scanDetail: Optional ClamAV scans run after checksum verification and before installation, including cached files. Missing definitions, scanner errors, detected threats and incomplete scans stop installation. Antivirus cannot guarantee safety.
privacy: Files stay on your computer. This option scans custom download files, not Steam credentials, saves, game folders or logs. Steam’s own updates are outside this scan step.
limits: Large, encrypted or unsupported archives can limit coverage. Reports say ‘no known threats detected within scanner limits’, not ‘safe’. Definitions must have been checked within seven days.
setupDetail: ClamAV is optional. Installation and definition updates open your local terminal. On Macs without Homebrew, installation opens ClamAV’s official download page. Definitions may need several hundred MB; scanning can take a while.
